inputs.drivers: Fixed-wireless and fibre competition; mobile penetration; churn and pricing; rural passings; DOCSIS; capex; refinancing; M&A synergies and deleveraging.
inputs.invalidation: Fixed wireless and fibre take durable share, ARPU weakens, capex and refinancing remain high, or merger dilution, preferred payments, and integration absorb free cash flow.
inputs.seed_claim: U.S. cable operators may defend fixed broadband through mobile convergence, simpler pricing, rural expansion, and upgrades, with convex equity upside and material leverage risk.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed requires slower internet losses, lower churn from mobile attach, maturing capex, and credible synergy and deleveraging progress.
inputs.value_chain: CHTR, CMCSA, CABO, and OPTU-like cable operators; TMUS, T, and VZ hedges; cable equipment and software; telecom credit.

objective: Research one cable-broadband convergence and leveraged-FCF investment idea.
